claims.text: A Ni-based interlayer can be used between W and CuCrZr in fusion-reactor plasma-facing modules.
Ni has a coefficient of thermal expansion intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
Ni has good compatibility with both W and CuCrZr.
A Ni-based interlayer will reduce stress at the W–CuCrZr interface under high thermal gradients.
A Ni-based interlayer will improve metallurgical bonding between W and CuCrZr.
A Ni-based layer can be applied to join W and CuCrZr using high-temperature brazing or diffusion bonding.
A thin Ni-based interlayer can accommodate the thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
Accommodation of thermal-expansion mismatch by the Ni interlayer mitigates thermally induced interfacial stress.
Stress mitigation by the Ni interlayer reduces crack propagation at the W–CuCrZr interface.
The Ni interlayer maintains sufficient W–CuCrZr joint strength at operating temperatures.
Compared with direct W–CuCrZr bonding, a Ni-based interlayer will reduce interfacial cracking or delamination.
Compared with direct W–CuCrZr bonding, a Ni-based interlayer will improve bonding integrity.
Direct bonding of W and CuCrZr can produce higher residual stress under high heat fluxes.
Direct bonding of W and CuCrZr can have suboptimal bond reliability under high heat fluxes.
The effectiveness of the Ni interlayer may depend on processing temperature and dwell time.
Long-term performance may be limited by the high-temperature stability of the Ni interlayer.
